newsitem.title: INDIA: India ONGC says to meet 96/97 crude output target.
newsitem.headline: India ONGC says to meet 96/97 crude output target.

text.p: India's state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd (ONGC) is likely to meet its total crude oil production target for the year ending March 31, 1997, a senior company official said on Monday.
"We hope to maintain our target," B.C. Bora, ONGC's chairman and managing director told Reuters after a news conference to announce a forthcoming conference on petroleum technology.
Bora said ONGC's target for 1996/97 was 29.3 million tonnes.

Analysts say ONGC's output for this fiscal year has so far been lagging from last fiscal year with April-November 1996 production reaching 19.169 million tonnes compared to 21.181 million tonnes in the same period last year.

The main cause has been the continuing fall in output at the country's largest hydrocarbon producing area, the Bombay High Basin, which fell to 1.643 million tonnes in November, a drop of 50,000 tonnes over October and nearly 200,000 tonnes from the same period last year.
